subject: Renewal: Dedicated cluster expansion & throughput SLO annex
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Carter <evelyn@nebulalabs.com>, procurement@nebulalabs.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: Dedicated cluster expansion & throughput SLO annex

Hi Evelyn / Nebula procurement team,

Thanks again for the productive renewal call last week. As discussed, Nebula is planning to expand the Dedicated cluster for the next 12-month term (additional 8 A100-equivalent GPUs) and wants clear throughput guarantees on the reserved pool that serves your high-throughput inference routes.

I attached a first draft of an SLA annex that captures: the tokens-per-second commitments for the new reserved pool, P95 latency baseline for 512-token requests, burst buffer behavior, and a credits formula in the event of under-delivery. Before I send to legal, can you confirm the following items so we align the wording: 
- Target steady-state throughput: 45,000 tokens/sec for the reserved pool (shared across two clusters)
- Peak burst: up to 75,000 tokens/sec for sustained 15-minute windows, subject to burst credits
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to a compatible quantized model variant with documented quality deltas

If those numbers look off, tell me the ranges Nebula needs and we can iterate. Our goal is to include the annex in the renewal amendment so the procurement and legal teams can sign one package.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: Nebula_Renewal_SLA_Annex_v1.pdf (SLA annex draft)

From: Evelyn Carter <evelyn@nebulalabs.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nebulalabs.com
Date: 2027-04-19T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated cluster expansion & throughput SLO annex

Jonas —

Appreciate the draft. High level: the GPU count and the idea of a tokens/sec guarantee make sense, but we need two clarifications before legal will engage on exact language:
1) Measurement window and attribution: Are tokens/sec measured per-second and evaluated on a daily rolling window, or over a 5-minute aggregation? We need determinism for our internal telemetry.
2) Credits calculation: We prefer a pragmatic formula that scales linearly with shortfalls, and a cap at one monthly invoice rather than a nominal credit.

Also, the fallback behavior is critical: if Redwood automatically routes to a quantized variant, what guardrails do we get on model quality (e.g., BLEU/EM/Rouge thresholds or sample outputs) and a guaranteed rollback window?

Procurement is OK with 8 additional GPUs but asks if you can tier the tokens/sec commitment to allow lower committed TPS in the first 30 days while we finish A/B tests.

Can you patch the annex to address the three bullets and send back?

—Evelyn
Evelyn Carter
Head of Platform Engineering, Nebula Labs
evelyn@nebulalabs.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Carter <evelyn@nebulalabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@nebulalabs.com
Date: 2027-04-20T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated cluster expansion & throughput SLO annex

Evelyn — thanks for the clear items. I updated the annex and summarized the changes inline below; updated draft attached (Nebula_Renewal_SLA_Annex_v1.pdf). Highlights: 

1) Measurement and windows
- Primary measurement: 1-second resolution token counters reported by our serving proxies, aggregated into a 5-minute rolling window for SLO evaluation.
- Compliance is judged on the 5-minute windows over a monthly billing cycle (i.e., percent of 5-min windows meeting TPS target).

2) Credits formula and caps
- Credit = (Committed_TPS - Actual_TPS)_avg_over_month / Committed_TPS * Monthly_pool_fee.
- Monthly cap: credits limited to 100% of the monthly reserved pool fee (will not exceed one month).
- Small shortfalls (<5% deviation for the month) are eligible for a 10% discretionary credit but not escalations.

3) Fallback, quality guards, and rollback
- Automatic fallback to the compatible quantized model (q8_compat) is permitted when sustained under-provisioning is detected for a sliding 15-minute window.
- Quality guardrails: sample-based drift checks with a default set of 50 prompt samples (we will share) and automatic rollback within 30 minutes if average quality delta (aggregate BLEU/ROUGE proxy) exceeds the negotiated threshold of 3 points.

4) Phased ramp for first 30 days
- For the initial 30-day ramp, committed TPS will be set to 65% of the long-term target (i.e., 29,250 TPS) to allow for A/B testing. Full commitment begins on day 31.

5) Observability and alerts
- We will grant Nebula a dedicated dashboard in Redwood Console with token-level telemetry, per-route p95 latency, and a weekly batch CSV export for audit.

Next steps: If that aligns, I can circulate the annex to our contracts team and have a DocuSign envelope ready. I've attached the redlines you can populate (Nebula_Redlines_v2.docx) and included a sample metric calculation in the annex.

Regards,
Jonas

Attachments: Nebula_Renewal_SLA_Annex_v1.pdf, Nebula_Redlines_v2.docx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: Dedicated cluster expansion & throughput SLO annex — negotiation notes (internal)

Marissa / Karthik —

Looping you both in with the latest from Nebula. They accepted the idea of the tokens/sec commitment but want: 1) a deterministic measurement window (we proposed 5-min rolling windows), 2) a linear credits formula with a monthly cap, and 3) a 30-day phased ramp to 100% commitment.

My suggested negotiation posture: accept the 5-minute rolling windows and the monthly cap (100% month credit), but push back on the 30-day ramp being too conservative — propose 14-day ramp at 80% (we can offer one-time free burst credits to help tests). Also, the automatic fallback rollback window: keep it at 30 minutes but require Nebula to accept exposure tests twice during pilot.

If legal asks about hard SLA penalties beyond credits, we should avoid uptime-style financials and keep remediation to credits + operational support (we can offer 20% discount on one month's pool fee instead of multi-month credits if they insist). Thoughts?

—Jonas

From: Evelyn Carter <evelyn@nebulalabs.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nebulalabs.com
Date: 2027-04-22T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated cluster expansion & throughput SLO annex

Jonas / Marissa —

Thanks for the detailed update and the revised annex. Nebula signs off on the 5-minute rolling window and the credits formula as written. Regarding ramp, procurement will accept a 14-day ramp to 80% provided we include a clause that grants Nebula two 30-minute orange-burst test windows where Redwood will provide unlimited burst capacity (subject to reasonable use) to validate production traffic.

We will route the annex and the renewal amendment to legal today. Please send the DocuSign link; procurement expects to wrap by end-of-week.

Acceptance: Nebula Labs approves the annex terms for inclusion in the renewal amendment.

—Evelyn
